test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 20 March, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e. '**Toppled'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3 is **"toppled".**
 
• **In the context of the sentence**, the man with the shotgun is being aggressive towards the guard, hence "toppled" makes sense because it suggests he forcefully knocked or pushed the guard onto the floor, especially given that this action followed a kick between the shoulder blades.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'The man with the shotgun pushed the guard to his knees. He handed up the shotgun to his partner and yanked the guard's wrists up behind his back and locked them together with a pair of handcuffs. He **toppled **him onto the floor with a kick between the shoulder blades. Then he took his shotgun back and (4) ______ to the security gate at the end of the counter. He was short and heavy and moved with peculiar slowness. “Buzz him (5) ______,” his partner said.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's why the other options are less suitable:
 
 
• **"Ascended"** means to rise or go up, which doesn't fit the context because the guard is being brought down, not lifted up.
 
• **"Placed" **is too gentle a word to describe the aggressive actions taking place.
 
• "**Straightened" **would imply the guard was being put upright or in a correct position, which again contradicts the aggressive context.
